name: Zac
bio:
Zac "ZacMuffin" Schuh is a {{wr:Any%}}-time world record holder in TCS Any%, the OG Season 3 Champion, and the defining figure of TCS speedrunning's modern era.

Zac began his career in late 2018 with Co-Op Episode 1 Wii Super Story runs, before eventually transitioning to Free Play Co-Op. After taking a long break, he returned in Spring of 2020, where he would begin seriously competing in main board categories. He set his first main board world record in the Free Play category in August of 2020, before beginning his Any% journey. After a tedious 300 hour grind in May-June of 2021, he achieved his first world record in Any% with a 2:28:28.

Shortly after his first world record, he won the OG Season 3 tournament without dropping a match, mounting a massive comeback against WiiSuper in Grand Finals. From then on, he held the world record for an impressive 1,285 out of 1,849 possible days, setting {{wr:Any%}} Any% world records along the way. Between January of 2022 and January of 2024, he would set a remarkable 20 world records, breaking 8 minute barriers in the process. This would mark one of the most dominant spells in the category's history, and create the foundation for his story in Summoning Salt's TCS documentary. During this period, he lost world record only three individual times, all to ERoadhouse, before taking a break and returning in 2025, where he would set an additional six records in a period of 7 months.

Zac has also won every BTR he has competed in, between the first 3 Any% BTRs and the only Free Play BTR. He is one of four runners to hold five or more main board world records simultaneously. His rivalry with ERoadhouse is one of the most notable in the game's history, playing a major role in Summoning Salt's TCS speedrunning documentary. Zac’s legacy is considered to be one of, if not the greatest runner in TCS Any% history.

Zac is known for his incredibly consistent playstyle, immense game knowledge, and his unprecedented ability to stay in top form without practice. His hobbies include speed typing, music, video editing, and soccer.

name: ERoadhouse
bio:
Evan “ERoadhouse” Rohde is a {{wr:Any%}}-time world record holder in TCS Any% and the Ladder League Season 1 Champion. Evan is renowned for setting the most history-defining world records in all of TCS Speedrunning.

Evan began speedrunning TCS in spring of 2020 for fun with friends before deciding to commit to taking the game seriously. Just months into his speedrunning career, he competed in the OG Season 2 tournament, finishing at an impressive 4th place. That August, after just five months of running, he achieved an Any% world record with his 2:39:43.

After Evan’s first Any% record, he battled back and forth with WiiSuper before finally setting a 2:34:51, marking the beginning of his dominant spell in Any%. In December, he achieved the most famous run in TCS history, a 2:31:49, finishing a remarkable 2 minutes and 9 seconds off of his sum of best.

In the summer of 2021, Evan achieved yet another staggering record with the first sub 2:30. His 2:29:57 would be his last record for over a year, as rivals Scynor and ZacMuffin would quickly rise to the top of the leaderboards following the discovery of the infamous DV2 Skip. Following a 3rd place finish in OG Season 3, he would take a break to make his mark on other categories.

Evan set his next Any% record during BTR 2022, where he fought directly with ZacMuffin in the game’s most storied rivalry. The pair combined to set all 22 consecutive records between June 2021 and June 2024, laying the groundwork for Summoning Salt’s TCS documentary. In late 2023, Evan broke the 9 hour barrier in 100%, becoming one of three runners to hold a world record in every main board category. In 2024, he won Ladder League Season 1 Grand Finals over itsjared97, taking down former champions ZacMuffin and Scynor in his path. Just days later, he broke the 2:20 barrier in Any% with a 2:19:08, his second 10 minute barrier and another monumental run.

Evan’s hybrid playstyle and near-perfect adaptability blends high top speed with consistency. He is notable for his ability to play for very long periods of time without making a single mistake. His hobbies include playing guitar, geography, Counter-Strike, and has a particular affinity for movies.

name: WiiSuper
bio:
Justin "WiiSuper" is a foundational TCS speedrunner from Pennsylvania. With a career spanning back nearly a decade, he is the game's most decorated speedrunner.

Justin began his speedrunning career in 2015 with casual Minecraft speedruns, before picking up TCS by random chance in November 2018. He, alongside his iconic rival Scynor, quickly rose to world record level, where he set his first Any% world record in March 2019 with a 3:03:09. Despite losing the race to sub 3, he quickly started one of the most dominant Any% reigns in the game's history. From April 2019 to October 2020, he set 22 world records, lowering his time by over 22 minutes, while only losing record a total of 4 times. After achieving a 2:36:08 in October 2020, he took a break, not achieving another world record until June 2024, the largest gap any runner has had between holding Any% world records.

Justin's staggering {{totalWRs}} world records across all categories, with dominant spells in All Minikits and 100%, is the most in the game's history. He also has achieved a board sweep, becoming the only runner besides Zulice to accomplish this. This was a feat he would repeat in September of 2020, becoming the only runner to ever achieve a board sweep on multiple separate occasions. Justin's many speedrun videos have garnered millions of views and have inspired numerous current top runners and eventual world record holders to begin competing.

Justin has the best average tournament finishing placement of any runner in the game's history, making it to Semifinals in every one of the 5 tournaments he has played in. Despite this, he has never been able to win a tournament, finishing as runner-up 3 times.

Justin is known for his strong consistency, smart playstyle, and ability to grind out finished runs. While Justin is no longer actively currently competing for the Any% world record, he is still active in speedrunning Minecraft and creating LEGO Star Wars YouTube content, such as LEGO Star Wars Geoguessr. Outside of speedrunning, he enjoys driving and geography.

name: Scynor
bio:
Sam “Scynor” Cynor is an {{wr:Any%}}-time Any% world record holder and the only two-time Any% tournament champion, winning OG Seasons 1 and 2. He is a titan of the game’s early competitive era.

Sam started playing TCS in December of 2018 after having some spare time following an appendectomy. He quickly rose to the top of the leaderboards, and set his first world record in Replay Story within a month. Two weeks later, he set his first Any% world record with a 3:09:16, marking the beginning of the “New Boys” era.

Sam’s historic rivalry with WiiSuper began to form as Sam would win the race to the game’s first Sub 3 hour run with a 2:58:50. This run would turn out to be a heavy focal point of Summoning Salt’s documentary on TCS Speedrunning. Later, Sam set world records in All Challenges, All Minikits, and 100%, completing one of the strongest years from any individual runner. In April of 2020, Sam bested WiiSuper in Grand Finals of the first TCS Any% tournament, simultaneously setting a world record with a 2:41:25. This remains the only time a world record has ever been set in a tournament, proving to be one of the greatest achievements in TCS history.

During the summer of 2020, Sam competed in the second season of the OG Any% tournament, coming in as a heavy favorite and dominating the competition, winning Grand Finals through the winner’s side against GingerLegend. In the spring of 2021, he battled against newer rivals ERoadhouse and ZacMuffin for the first sub 2:30. He would ultimately lose the race, but with the help of the new DV2 and Library skips, he achieved the second sub 2:30 and a new world record of 2:29:37.

In addition to being the only player to compete in all six Any% tournaments, he has impressively reached the playoffs stage in every iteration. His unmatched raw speed has always put him a step ahead of the other competitors, making him a title threat in every season. Coupled with his 2 trophies, Sam’s tournament resume is among the greatest ever.

Sam is known for his unbridled talent, prowess in races, and incredibly strong early games. His hobbies include cycling, soccer, and golf, as well as playing competitive chess and poker.

name: Bricko
bio:
Bricko Fett is the Ladder League Season 3 Champion and an accomplished TCS Veteran. He began speedrunning the game in November of 2020 and quickly improved in Any% after discovering the run through WiiSuper's Gonk% runs on youtube.

He competed in the OG Season 3 tournament in 2021 and made Top 8 relatively early into his speedrunning career. After this, he would take a break from tournaments until 2026.

Bricko achieved a 2:27 during BTR 2022, finding himself on record pace for the first time in his career into the final two episodes. Over the coming years, he would achieve multiple 2nd place runs on the leaderboard. He has been a mainstay of the top 4 for years since his breakthrough in Any%, and has branched out to other categories such as All Minikits, in which he achieved {{wr:All Minikits}} world records and broke a 10 minute barrier with a 3:38.

In late 2025, he returned to Any% with the goal of becoming the next Ladder League Champion. After a tumultuous ladder stage, he won the tournament as the 7 seed, besting the favored 1 seed Dragon in Grand Finals with a 2:19:19. This made Bricko the first runner to win a TCS tournament despite having never held an Any% world record.

Bricko is known for his highly resilient mentality, drive to grind and improve, and impressive top speed. His hobbies include film photography, speedcubing, geoguessr, LEGO collecting, movies, and cars.

name: Jared
bio:
Jared “itsjared97” Hyman is a {{wr:Any%}}-time world record holder in TCS Any% and the Ladder League Season 2 Champion. An accomplished runner from the post-Covid era, Jared is one of the most mechanically sound players ever.

Jared discovered TCS through WiiSuper’s 100% speedruns, and completed his first Any% run in February of 2020. He quickly broke into the top 10 and competed in the OG Season 2 tournament, finishing in 5th place. Throughout the remainder of the year, he picked up other categories, eventually completing his first 100% run in August. The following year, his Round 2 exit of the OG Season 3 tournament would result in a brief hiatus from speedrunning until 2022, where he would return to achieve Sub 2:30 and compete in BTR 2022.

Jared continued running at a high level in the following years, but didn’t fully hit his stride until 2024. He obtained his first main board world record with a 59:18 in Prequels in February. In June, he achieved his first Any% world record, a 2:21:17, while in the midst of Ladder League Season 1. A loss to ERoadhouse in Grand Finals marked his finish as runner-up, but Jared continued to stay at world record level over the coming months. With the discovery of God Fraud and FRY Skip, he achieved his second Any% world record with a 2:18:35 in March of 2025. Jared rode this momentum through Ladder League Season 2, beating WiiSuper in a tense Grand Finals to become the new champion, capping off the best year of his speedrunning career.

Despite multiple shaky tournament starts, Jared has made playoffs in every Ladder League season and reached the Grand Finals stage in two of them. His dedication and strength when his back is against the wall are world class, and he credits that toughness to his time playing college baseball. His achievements have built him a fantastic resume that has etched him into TCS history.

Jared is known for his relentless grinding, uncapped mechanical potential, ability to perform under pressure in tournaments, and early game expertise. His hobbies include cooking, raving about sports, composing music, and playing with his cats.

name: Dragon76
bio:
Severi “Dragon76” is a {{wr:Any%}}-time world record holder in TCS Any% and one of the most mechanically skilled players in history. His immense passion for the game combined with improbable skill at a young age has made him the pioneer of the new generation.

Dragon started running TCS in August of 2024. His improvement rate was rapid, achieving Sub 2:30 in just four months. His intense grind at the start of his career would catapult him to just outside of the top 10 heading into Ladder League Season 2. He qualified for playoffs as the eight seed, and pulled off arguably the greatest tournament upset ever, defeating heavy favorite FrostByte in Quarterfinals. He would finish his first tournament in third place, a strong debut that clearly showcased his immense potential.

He continued his grind into the off-season, before breaking through in March of 2026 with his 2:17:47, skipping 2:18 and 2:19. One month later, he would attain his first Any% world record with a 2:17:02, becoming the first European to hold an Any% world record since TSG in 2018.

Dragon would showcase his talent further by qualifying as the one seed for Ladder League Season 3 Playoffs. After flying into the US from Finland, he won close matches in Quarterfinals and Semifinals against previous tournament winners itsjared97 and ZacMuffin. His first loss arrived at the hands of Bricko in Grand Finals, finishing as runner-up. Bouncing back from the tournament loss, he claimed his second Any% world record and the game’s first 2:15 just five days later.

Dragon is known for his intense dedication, unrestrained top speed, and fierce practice habits. His hobbies include speedcubing, geography, and running.

name: Anorak
bio:
David “Anorak” is one of the highest level Any% runners of the new generation. He started learning the game at the end of 2022 after watching Summoning Salt’s “The History of Lego Star Wars World Records.”

David has competed in all three installments of Ladder League. After only running the game seriously for a few months, he placed 22nd in season 1. His off-season improvements lead to a significantly better performance in season 2, as he qualified to playoffs as the seven seed. After his elimination in Quarterfinals, he took a brief break, before returning the following year. David worked his way into the top 5 for the first time in January of 2026. The following season, his ladder performances drastically improved, and he qualified to playoffs emphatically early with the three seed. Despite his eventual loss to WiiSuper in Quarterfinals, his continued improvement across the game has allowed him to rise to world record level.

He has also played an important role in recent optimizations of the game, finding small timesaves, setups, backups, and inspiring other runners through competition. His extended game knowledge rivals only ZacMuffin’s, and has sharpened his adaptability as a highly useful tool. While David has yet to achieve his first world record, he has peaked at 4th place multiple times, and his commitment to playing Any% consistently since he began running is unparalleled.

David’s playstyle easily translates to other speedgames, of which he has run several at a high level. He has notable times in Super Mario 64, Minecraft, and Black Ops 3 Zombies, as well as top 10 times in Outer Wilds.

David is known for his game knowledge, problem solving, and dedication to practice. His interests include conservation biology, evolutionary biology, astronomy, and pencil drawing, among other art forms.
